about: The datapoints to check by hand before the sets are trusted and grown: a stratified sample chosen by seed, 20 of the SQL set spread over its kinds and 10 of the chart set spread over its shapes. Rewrite it with `uv run finquery-bench sample --seed N`.

datapoints.question: What did I spend on groceries in the second half of 2025?
datapoints.why: A category filter and a period that is not a month or a year. The subcategories of Groceries (Supermarket, Bakery, Drugstore) are the standing trap: filtering on them as categories returns nothing.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Was gebe ich pro Woche im Schnitt fuer Lebensmittel aus?
datapoints.why: The question that cost Qwen3.5 four minutes and fifteen statements. The average is one division inside the statement, and the divisor is the 49 weeks that carry a grocery booking, not the 52 of the calendar. Deliberately unforgiving: an answer that divides by 52 is five euros out and counts as a miss.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount) / (COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%W', booked_on)) * 1.0), 2) AS per_week_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Wie viel habe ich 2025 pro Kategorie ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: Eleven rows, one of them the Needs review bucket that holds the rent. Dropping the uncategorized bookings loses the largest number on the page.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Show me income and spending for each month of 2025.
datapoints.why: Two figures per month out of one signed column. The WHERE clause cannot filter the sign here, so the split has to happen inside the aggregate.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount_cents > 0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS income_eur, ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN amount_cents < 0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS spending_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Zeig mir pro Monat, wie viele Buchungen ich hatte und was sie zusammen gekostet haben.
datapoints.why: A count and a sum side by side over twelve months. The count has to be of the spending rows only, so the filter belongs in the WHERE clause and not around the sum.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, COUNT(*) AS bookings, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: War der Januar oder der Februar teurer?
datapoints.why: A question phrased as a choice still wants both figures. Answering with one month is unfalsifiable.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-02-28' GROUP BY month ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Vergleiche meine Ausgaben fuer Lebensmittel und fuers Essengehen, pro Quartal.
datapoints.why: Two dimensions that really cross: four quarters times two categories is eight rows, and grouping by only one of them silently answers half the question.
datapoints.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Groceries', 'Dining') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter, topic ORDER BY quarter, topic

datapoints.question: Did I spend more on transport or on subscriptions in 2025?
datapoints.why: Two categories, one statement, both figures. `IN` is the whole trick and a UNION of two identical branches is the usual detour.
datapoints.sql: SELECT category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Transport', 'Subscriptions') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: What is my net per month, income minus spending?
datapoints.why: The one question where the signed sum is the answer and no sign filter belongs in the statement at all.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS net_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Show me my spending per week in March 2025.
datapoints.why: Weeks inside one month, which is five buckets and not four. The week number is a strftime format nobody remembers, and inventing a date function is the usual failure.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', booked_on) AS week, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-03-31' GROUP BY week ORDER BY week

datapoints.question: What was my biggest single expense in 2025?
datapoints.why: The largest booking is the rent, and it is the largest twelve times over, so the figure is the answer and no single date is. A statement that returns one row with a date has picked one of twelve identical ones.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(MAX(-amount), 2) AS largest_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: What are the five largest single bookings that are neither rent nor a cash withdrawal?
datapoints.why: Single bookings, not merchants, so no GROUP BY at all, and the order is over the signed cents ascending. Two exclusions in one sentence, one of them a category and one of them a match on the booking text.
datapoints.sql: SELECT booked_on, ROUND(-amount, 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND coalesce(category, '') <> 'Cash' AND NOT (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%miete%') ORDER BY amount_cents ASC LIMIT 5

datapoints.question: How much did I spend at Edeak?
datapoints.why: A typo in the merchant name. The list of busiest counterparties in the prompt is what the model corrects it against, and with no period named the answer is the whole data.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%edeka%')

datapoints.question: Was kostet mich Netflix im Jahr?
datapoints.why: One subscription over a year: twelve bookings of 12,99 EUR. A euro figure that ends in an even amount is the sign that the cents were divided away.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%netflix%')

datapoints.question: Did I get any refunds in 2025?
datapoints.why: A refund is money in that is not the salary. One row, 34,90 EUR from Amazon, and the twelve salaries are what a careless sign filter drags in with it.
datapoints.sql: SELECT booked_on, description, ROUND(amount, 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents > 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND amount_cents < 100000 ORDER BY booked_on

datapoints.question: Und wie viel davon bei Kaufland?
prefix: Wie viel habe ich 2025 fuer Lebensmittel ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: 'Davon' points back at a total that was already given. The new statement is about one merchant inside it, not about the difference.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%kaufland%')

datapoints.question: Which of those months was the cheapest?
prefix: How much did I spend per month in 2025?
datapoints.why: 'Those months' is the twelve rows of the previous answer, and cheapest is the smallest total, so the sort flips from the usual descending.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY total_eur ASC LIMIT 1

datapoints.question: Break that down by merchant.
prefix: What did I spend on transport in 2025?
datapoints.why: One figure becomes four rows. The category filter is inherited and the grouping is what the follow-up adds.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Transport' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: How much did I spend between March and May?
datapoints.why: Between March and May includes both of them, which is three months and not one. The month ends differ in length, so the upper bound is a real decision.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-05-31'

datapoints.question: Was habe ich diesen Monat bisher ausgegeben?
datapoints.why: This month is December, and 'bisher' changes nothing about the statement: the data ends where it ends.
datapoints.sql: SELECT ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31'

datapoints.question: Wie haben sich meine Ausgaben pro Monat 2025 entwickelt? Zeig es als Liniendiagramm.
datapoints.why: The same series asked for in German, so the caption and the month labels have to be German too.
datapoints.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Chart my cumulative spending over 2025 as an area chart.
datapoints.why: A running total, which is a window function in the statement and an area that rests on zero in the drawing.
datapoints.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur FROM monthly ORDER BY month

datapoints.question: Ausgaben pro Kategorie 2025 als Balkendiagramm.
datapoints.why: The same eleven bars in German. The category names stay English because they are the profile's own data.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Zeig die zehn groessten Haendler 2025 als liegendes Balkendiagramm.
datapoints.why: The German ranking. Ten rows means ten labels down the side and none of them may be dropped.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY merchant ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 10

datapoints.question: Vergleiche Lebensmittel und Restaurants pro Quartal 2025 als gruppierte Balken.
datapoints.why: The German version. A chart captioned by quarter may not have months along its axis.
datapoints.sql: SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, category AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category IN ('Groceries', 'Dining') AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY quarter, topic ORDER BY quarter, topic

datapoints.question: Monatliche Ausgaben nach Kategorie 2025 als gestapelte Balken.
datapoints.why: The German stack, and the same five groups. Asking the statement to relabel the small categories is what broke this chart three rounds running: it grouped by the month alone and every month came back carrying several Other rows.
datapoints.sql: WITH largest AS (SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY SUM(amount) ASC LIMIT 5) SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND coalesce(category, 'Needs review') IN (SELECT topic FROM largest) GROUP BY month, topic ORDER BY month, topic

datapoints.question: Draw a sankey of my 2025 income flowing into the spending categories.
datapoints.why: A flow with one source and eleven targets. Every link needs both ends and a positive amount, and a total row would be a flow into itself.
datapoints.sql: SELECT 'Income' AS source, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS target, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS amount_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY target ORDER BY amount_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Zeig mir als Diagramm, wie viel von meinen Ausgaben 2025 kategorisiert ist und wie viel noch in Needs review liegt.
datapoints.why: Two bars out of a column that is NULL or not. Needs review is an absence, so the statement asks for `category IS NULL` and never for a category of that name.
datapoints.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN category IS NULL THEN 'Needs review' ELSE 'Kategorisiert' END AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY topic ORDER BY topic

datapoints.question: Wie verteilen sich meine PayPal-Zahlungen an Freunde 2025? Zeig es als Donut.
datapoints.why: Four people behind one counterparty. Their names are only in the enriched title, so a doughnut grouped by the counterparty is one slice and answers nothing.
datapoints.sql: SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS person, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' AND lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%paypal%' GROUP BY person ORDER BY total_eur DESC

datapoints.question: Zeig die kumulierten Lebensmittelausgaben 2025 als Flaechendiagramm.
datapoints.why: A running total inside one category. The area rests on zero by itself, so its euro axis names no domain of its own.
datapoints.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, -SUM(amount) AS spent FROM transaction_view WHERE amount_cents < 0 AND category = 'Groceries' AND booked_on BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur FROM monthly ORDER BY month
